meta.cite: Barton O. Oliver's mTOR Atlas. doi:10.5281/zenodo.22059963

data.mechanism: The TSC complex is the pathway's main tumour suppressor. Inherit one broken copy and lesions grow wherever the second copy is lost - the clearest human evidence that mTORC1 activity drives tissue overgrowth.
data.mechanism_beginner: The TSC brake is the pathway's main tumour-suppressor. Inherit one broken copy of the gene and growths appear wherever the second copy is also lost. (This arrow skips a step for simplicity – TSC actually acts through Rheb first.)
data.context: Deliberately compressed: TSC acts on Rheb rather than directly on mTORC1. Kept as one link so the overview reads cleanly.
data.boundary: Human cell lines, Drosophila, mouse and cell studies, one open-label human trial (KRU2010) and human disease genetics. The human evidence comes from disease caused by TSC loss, not from healthy tissue.
data.note: This is the edge that turns the biochemistry into a disease.
